messages:
chris: Quick question — for the v1->v2 migration, can we land a small runtime escape hatch that toggles per-route version routing (so we can revert a tenant without a full deploy)?

chris: Thinking: a runtime flag on route metadata + api-gateway honouring it. fallback rule still routes to v1 if enabled.

tian: +1 for escape hatch. We also need to decide how quotas map during the window. If v2 token accounting differs (e.g. different prompt expansion), customers could get surprised.

kelly: From Console POV we should show an inline banner per-route: "Serving: v2 (fallback to v1 enabled)" and an CTA to run a dry-run to compare cost/latency. :eyes:

maya: UX note — don't spam tenants with banners during rollout. Maybe show banner only when a tenant actually hits the v2 path (sampled) or if they visit the route config.

chris: Agreed. Implementation sketch: runtime flag (route.override_version), telemetry events when a request is routed to v2/v1, and a sampled "migration-diff" event that attaches token delta. Example header we add for routing/debug: `X-Redwood-Served-Version: v2|v1`

chris: config example: `{"route_id":"/payments/charge","override_version":"v1"}`

tian: For telemetry we need three signals: version header (always), route-override (boolean), and effective_token_delta (sampled). This allows billing/product to show estimated cost impact.

kelly: Console would love a small breakdown: avg latency v1 vs v2, avg tokens/req v1 vs v2, and %requests using fallback. We can run a 1% shadow cohort to get those numbers.

maya: Important: rollout plan needs two safety knobs — (1) per-tenant escape hatch, (2) global emergency revert. Both should be callable from Console + infra API.

chris: Ops concern: revert must not blow up quota charge calculations. If we switch back and forth, billing signals should be stable. We should emit a routed_version tag in billing pipeline so downstream can map usage to the right pricing profile.

sourabh: On quotas: we might apply a grace-mapping for the window: map v2 usage to v1 quota buckets 1:1 for N days, then reconcile. Requires a reconciliation job that diffs sampled token deltas. If reconciliation finds >5% delta we notify billing/product.

kelly: Console UX for reconciliation alerts: per-tenant flag showing "quota-reconciled | pending" and a one-click download of sampled diffs.

maya: Also commit to a migration SLA: if a tenant sees >30% cost increase vs baseline we auto-flag and notify SE. Don't auto-revert without consent.

chris: Implementation tasks I see:
- runtime: route.override_version flag + gateway honour
- telemetry: add X-Redwood-Served-Version, route.override boolean, sampled token_delta event
- billing: routed_version tag and a reconciliation job
- console: per-route banner + dry-run reports + escape hatch UI

chris: question: how do we sample token_delta without overloading tracing? keep sample rate tiny (0.1%) and correlate by route+tenant.

tian: 0.1% seems fine. We'll aggregate on ingest side and only store summaries. Also emit counters for total token estimates so we can compute extrapolated impact without storing all samples.

sourabh: For emergency revert we should add a circuit-breaker that can be triggered by a metric rule (latency or token_cost_up) and call the runtime API to flip overrides. Circuit-breaker should record reason and who triggered it.

kelly: We'll need Console audit entries for circuit-breaker usage. ops people will want to see when and why reverts happened.

deploy-bot: deploy: feature/route-override added runtime flag support to staging — build #2024.

chris: Nice. Can staging run a simulated reconciliation to validate the pipeline?

tian: Yes, will run a dry ingestion against staging logs tomorrow.

maya: Action items:
- chris: prototype runtime flag + gateway honour (PR)
- tian: add telemetry fields + sampling plan
- kelly: console banner + dry-run UI mockups (keep non-annoying thresholds)
- sourabh: circuit-breaker runbook + reconciliation job spec

chris: timeline: aim for shadow cohort + console dry-run in 2 weeks, 1% roll in 4 weeks if numbers look OK.

kelly: I'll mock the UI and put screenshots in the design review doc.

maya: Sounds good. Keep comms light to customers — announce migration window + opt-out path.

sourabh: One more: if we do per-route escape hatch, validate we don't create tenant isolation that bypasses security checks. We'll run an ACL test matrix.

chris: Good call. I'll add that to PR checklist.

maya: Thanks all — we'll sync again at the weekly platform sync. :thumbsup:
